sections.h2: Where is Waterloo and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Waterloo is the Black Hawk County seat in northeast Iowa, and the Cedar River splits it into eastern and western halves. Cedar Falls, the home of the University of Northern Iowa, sits next door as its twin city.

The 2020 census counted 67,314 people, which made Waterloo the eighth-largest city in Iowa. The wider metro area, covering Black Hawk, Bremer and Grundy counties, has about 170,000 residents. Smaller communities around the city include Evansdale, Hudson, Raymond, Elk Run Heights, Gilbertville and Washburn, and buyers shopping for a house often compare Waterloo with those places and with Cedar Falls.

sections.h2: What shaped Waterloo's housing and its economy?
sections.html:
Factory work built this city. The settlement started as Prairie Rapids Crossing in 1845 and took the name Waterloo when Charles Mullan petitioned for a post office. The city incorporated in 1868, and population jumped from 8,490 in 1895 to 33,097 in 1915.

The Waterloo Gasoline Engine Company began making tractors in 1893 under the Waterloo Boy name, and Rath Packing moved in during that growth period, which is why Waterloo is called the Factory City. Much of the older housing in the city likely traces to those decades of growth.

The boom did not hold evenly. John Deere cut about 10,000 jobs in the 1980s farm recession and now employs roughly a third of its peak workforce, with more layoffs in 2024 and 2025. The Rath plant closed in the 1980s, taking about 2,500 jobs, and the city lost an estimated 14 percent of its population that decade. Owners who have held houses through all of that often face a mix of older homes and slower appreciation.

sections.html:

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Waterloo homeowners?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau reports a 62.1 percent owner-occupied rate and a median home value of $152,600 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $923, and the median household income is $57,480 in 2024 dollars.

  • Persons per household: 2.25
  • Bachelor's degree or higher, ages 25 and up: 21.8 percent
  • Mean travel time to work: 15.9 minutes

About 38 percent of occupied homes are not owner-occupied, so a fair share of the houses on any given block may be landlord-owned. That can shape who your neighbors are and who might buy your house.

sections.h2: Can the Cedar River flood a Waterloo house?
sections.html:
Yes, and the 2008 flood is the benchmark. The June 2008 event was the largest on record in the Waterloo and Cedar Falls area, with a peak discharge of 112,000 cubic feet per second at the Waterloo gage on June 11. The Great Flood of 1993 was another major event.

The city has since put money into its levees. After the Army Corps identified deficiencies in 2016, Waterloo spent just over $8 million on two phases of upgrades, finished in 2022 and 2024, and the system is again eligible for federal flood protection programs. An October 2025 report said the East and Northwest segments were fully compliant and the Southwest segment was due to finish by the end of 2025.

Ask your insurance agent whether your address is mapped inside a floodplain, since that affects what a financed buyer must carry. A cash buyer can skip that lender requirement.

sections.h2: What is the climate in Waterloo, and what does it do to a roof and furnace?
sections.html:
Waterloo has a humid continental climate with a 154-day growing season. Monthly mean temperatures range from 18.5 degrees F in January to 73.6 degrees F in July, and the record low is minus 34 degrees F, reached in 1962 and again in 2009.

Normal annual precipitation is about 34.6 inches, with heavier rain in spring and summer, and winter snowfall averages 35.3 inches. Spring melt and heavy rain are the seasons to watch for basement moisture. With winters that cold, buyers tend to look closely at furnace age and attic insulation.

sections.h2: What rules apply to Waterloo rental owners who want to sell?
sections.html:
Waterloo requires registration of every rental unit, even a vacant one. The program applies to dwellings that are not eligible for the Iowa homestead credit and are not the owner's home, and landlords must name a responsible local agent.

Rental registration itemWaterloo rule
Fee$25 per unit
Late feeRises to $50 per unit on January 1
Annual deadlineNovember 1, for a permit running January 1 to December 31
Newly purchased propertyRegister within 30 days of purchase

The city's page does not say what happens to a seller's registration at a sale, so ask the City Clerk at 319-291-4323 before you close. The 30-day rule means the new owner will need to register right away.

sections.h2: What help does the city offer for repairs, and how does that compare with an as-is sale?
sections.html:
Waterloo Community Development runs owner-occupied rehabilitation, emergency repair, Healthy Homes and lead hazard programs, plus rental rehabilitation loans and down payment help for qualifying buyers. The office is at 620 Mulberry Street, Suite 202, and its number is 319-291-4429.

Those programs are worth a call if you plan to stay. If you plan to leave, the question is whether repair funding and contractor time fit your timeline. Eligibility rules and award amounts are not listed on the city's page, so confirm them directly.

sections.h2: What schools, colleges and hospitals are in Waterloo?
sections.html:
The Waterloo Community School District covers nearly the entire city. Its public high schools are Waterloo West, Waterloo East and Expo High School, and private options include Waterloo Christian School and Columbus Catholic High School.

Hawkeye Community College is in Waterloo, and the University of Northern Iowa is a short drive away in Cedar Falls. Two hospitals anchor the health sector: MercyOne Waterloo Medical Center with 366 beds and UnityPoint Allen Memorial Hospital with 234 beds. Those institutions give the city a steady base of staff, students and families who need housing near campus or work.

sections.h2: How do property tax and transfer tax work when selling in Waterloo?
sections.html:
Black Hawk County bills in two halves. September 1 is the first due date and taxes go delinquent after September 30, and March 1 is the second due date with delinquency after March 31. Interest runs 1.5 percent per month, and the annual tax sale is held on the third Monday of June.

The Iowa transfer tax is 80 cents per $500 of value after the first $500, with any fraction counted as a full $500 step. On the county median of $152,600, that comes to $244.00 by our math. A declaration of value goes to the county recorder with the deed.

Roads and transit matter to buyers too. Interstate 380 ends at Waterloo, U.S. 20, 63 and 218 and Iowa 21 serve the area, and the Metropolitan Transit Authority of Black Hawk County runs local buses Monday through Saturday.

faqs.q: Do Waterloo landlords have to register a rental before selling it?
faqs.a: Yes, while you own it. Registration is $25 per unit, due November 1, and it applies even if the unit is empty. The buyer must register within 30 days of purchase.

faqs.q: When are Black Hawk County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Unpaid first-half taxes are delinquent after September 30 and second-half after March 31.

faqs.q: Is Waterloo still at risk of Cedar River flooding?
faqs.a: Some risk remains. The city finished about $8 million in levee upgrades in 2022 and 2024, but your own address may still sit in a mapped floodplain, so check with your insurance agent.

faqs.q: What is a typical home value in Waterloo?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists a median value of $152,600 for owner-occupied homes from 2020 to 2024. Your own house can sit well above or below that depending on condition and location.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Waterloo house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as-is, list it for a buyer who plans to renovate, or use a city repair program if you qualify and plan to stay.
